script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The comparison between standing firm and being loud is confusing. The idea that whispered freedom is easy to push around does not clarify Paul's instruction.
The discount joke appears on a card about circumcision. Cards about the body's private matters have no joke.
The bonus-round joke appears on a card about circumcision. Cards about the body's private matters have no joke.
Calling the question a trap jokes about the choice card, and the cookie-bill joke appears on a card about circumcision.
One step into the law makes a broader claim than Paul does. He says the man who gets himself circumcised is obligated to obey the whole law.
The quotation stops before the end of Paul's sentence without an ellipsis.

The quotation from Galatians 5:5 stops before the hope of righteousness without an ellipsis.
Paul says the persuasion does not come from the One who calls them. Saying whatever slows them down does not come from Him is broader than the text.

The cookies-eating-each-other joke makes light of Paul's serious warning about people harming one another.

explanations.explanation: Paul says it right after the freedom line: "Stand firm, then…" (Galatians 5:1). Christ already did the setting free, so the baker's part is to plant both feet and hold the spot. I picture myself on my gold base while somebody tries to scoot me off the counter. Not today, friend.

explanations.answer: Work hard to earn their freedom
explanations.explanation: Nope, friend, nobody earns this one. Paul says Christ has set them free (Galatians 5:1), and a gift that's already handed over doesn't need a payment plan. What Paul asks for is to stand firm. That's holding on to the gift, not working for it.

Paul never says to hush up about it. He says, "Stand firm, then…" (Galatians 5:1), and standing firm is a pretty loud way to stand. I think a freedom you whisper about is a freedom that's easy to push around. Paul wants them planted.

Yes, Paul warns them not to be "encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). Notice the words "once more." They'd been under that weight before, and he doesn't want them picking it back up. I know a little about being stuck under a heavy pile, and I did NOT enjoy it.

It's actually true, friend. Paul says, "do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery" (Galatians 5:1). A yoke is a heavy wooden frame that goes on the shoulders, so he's warning them about a weight they shouldn't take back on. Christ set them free, and Paul doesn't want them strapping the load on again.

That's it. Paul says that if they let themselves be circumcised, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2). Not a little less. Not a discount. NONE. Paul doesn't leave himself any wiggle room there.

I can see why that sounds like a bonus round, but Paul says the opposite. If they let themselves be circumcised, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2). It's not an add-on that makes Christ bigger. Paul says it takes the value of Christ away from them.

If only it were that simple, friend. Paul says, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2). He doesn't say the same, and he doesn't say a little less. He says none, and he puts his own name on it.

Careful, friend, this one's a trap. Paul says a man who gets himself circumcised "is obligated to obey the whole law" (Galatians 5:3). It's the whole thing, not one command. It's like thinking you ordered just one cookie and getting handed the entire bakery bill.
Right, it's false. Paul says that man "is obligated to obey the whole law" (Galatians 5:3). That's every command, not just one. One step into the law and Paul says the whole law comes with it.

explanations.answer: They have been severed from Christ
explanations.explanation: That's what Paul says: "You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ" (Galatians 5:4). Severed is a strong word, like a clean cut. Paul isn't tiptoeing around, and I'm not going to soften it either.

explanations.answer: They have drawn closer to Christ
explanations.explanation: You'd think more effort would mean more closeness, but Paul says the opposite. Those trying to be justified by the law "have been severed from Christ" (Galatians 5:4). Severed means cut off, not pulled in. Trying to earn it by the law ends up pushing them away from Christ.

Grace doesn't work like a rewards card, friend. Paul says those trying to be justified by the law "have fallen away from grace" (Galatians 5:4). So instead of piling up extra, they've drifted away from it. Grace is a gift, and you can't stack it by trying harder.

Yes! Paul says, "by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5). Faith is what he leans on, and the Spirit is the One he waits through. I know a little about waiting, and faith makes it a whole lot lighter.

Close to the topic, but it's the very thing Paul has been pushing back on. Those trying to be justified by the law have "fallen away from grace" (Galatians 5:4). So when he turns to how he and the believers wait, he says, "by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit" (Galatians 5:5). Faith is the word that fits.

I love a hard worker, friend, but that's not the word here. Paul says, "by faith we eagerly await through the Spirit the hope of righteousness" (Galatians 5:5). He doesn't point to effort at all. He points to faith, and to the Spirit.

That's the one. "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). Faith isn't just sitting in the heart. It shows up and gets to work in love. Same as a good cookie: it's not enough to LOOK nice, somebody has to be able to eat it.

That sounds responsible, but it isn't what Paul says. He says, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). Back in verse 3 he already reminded them that circumcision brings an obligation to obey the whole law. Perfect command-keeping isn't what he says matters here. Faith working through love is.

explanations.answer: Coming from the right family line
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn't bring up family lines here at all. He says neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any value, and then, "What matters is faith expressing itself through love" (Galatians 5:6). Faith is what matters. Where you come from isn't on his list.

Not quite, friend. Paul says, "Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you" (Galatians 5:8). So the persuasion doesn't come from God. Whatever is slowing them down, it isn't coming from Him.
Right, it's false. Paul says, "Such persuasion does not come from the One who calls you" (Galatians 5:8). The One who calls them isn't the source of it. Paul says it plain.

Yes! "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). Leaven is what makes dough rise, and Paul says even a little spreads through all of it. Friend, I've seen it happen on my counter, and the dough does not ask permission.
Not the top layer, friend. Paul says, "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). It doesn't stay on the surface. A little goes all the way through.
That would be a very polite leaven, but Paul says otherwise. "A little leaven works through the whole batch of dough" (Galatians 5:9). It doesn't stay in one spot. It spreads through the whole batch.
That's right. Paul says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). Notice the "whoever he may be." Paul doesn't name him, so I won't guess either.

explanations.answer: He will be let off free
explanations.explanation: Paul doesn't say that. He says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). So he doesn't get a pass. And since Paul doesn't say who he is, I'll leave that open too.

explanations.answer: He will be put in charge
explanations.explanation: Nope, no promotion here. Paul says, "The one who is troubling you will bear the judgment, whoever he may be" (Galatians 5:10). Judgment is the word, not leadership. Nobody's getting a bigger apron for this.

It's the other way around, friend. Paul's "if" matters: "if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?" (Galatians 5:11). He's asking a question, not admitting anything. In his reasoning, the persecution is a sign that he isn't preaching it.

Right. Paul says, "if I am still preaching circumcision, why am I still being persecuted?" (Galatians 5:11). That "if" is doing the work. He asks it as a question, and he isn't admitting that he still preaches it.

Yes! Paul says, "you, brothers, were called to freedom; but do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh" (Galatians 5:13). Freedom comes with a warning label. I think of it like a big open kitchen: lovely to have, and there's still a way to use it well.

Paul does warn them, friend. He says, "do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh" (Galatians 5:13). They were called to freedom, and the warning comes right along with it. Then he says what to do instead: "serve one another in love."

That's the one. "The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself'" (Galatians 5:14). The whole law, in one line. That's a recipe card I can actually fit in my apron pocket.
That's a real command, friend. It's in Exodus 20:8. But it isn't the one Paul picks here. He says the entire law is fulfilled in this single decree: "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Galatians 5:14).
That's a real command too, found in Exodus 20:12. But Paul names a different one. He says, "The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree: 'Love your neighbor as yourself'" (Galatians 5:14).

Yes. Paul warns, "if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). Biting and devouring ends with being consumed. Friend, nobody wins when the cookies start eating each other.

Good guess, but that's not Paul's word. He says, "if you keep on biting and devouring one another, watch out, or you will be consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). It's consumed, like what happens when you keep devouring. He doesn't say anything about scattering.

Not shamed, friend. Paul says, "watch out, or you will be consumed by one another" (Galatians 5:15). The picture is biting and devouring, so the end of it is being consumed. Paul keeps the picture going to the end.
